about:
Classic Sheet Metal was founded in March 1962 in a 7,500-square-foot facility in Chicago, Illinois. The company relocated to Schiller Park in the late 1960s, then to a 30,000-square-foot plant where it operated for three decades before moving to its current headquarters in Addison, Illinois, in 2000. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides turnkey sheet metal fabrication including CNC punching, laser cutting, stamping, forming, welding, and contract assembly. It runs both short-run (custom or urgent turnaround) and long-run production, with stated capacity ranging from prototype quantities to several million pieces annually. The facility operates under an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system and employs statistical process control (SPC) with decades of accumulated process data.

Classic Sheet Metal serves as a supply-chain partner for several well-known global companies across a broad geographic footprint that includes the Midwest, South, and Mountain West regions. Specific industry sectors or named customers are not disclosed in public materials.

The firm was established on the premise that quality and customer service are the cornerstones of excellence. It differentiates itself through early adoption of SPC, a Virtek Laser QC automated inspection system capable of ±0.05 mm accuracy, and a suite of quality tools including PPAP, FMEA, Six Sigma, and just-in-time delivery programs.
